rows.question: I've got a cashback deal and a bonus-data deal - can both be applied when I top up once?
rows.answer: Here is what the retrieved documents say: "If not, raise a ticket under Billing > Report Issue with both transaction references; approved refunds are credited to the original payment method or as account balance" [D1]. "Auto-detection is the default path (3-5 working days), and the manual ticket route exists specifically as the fallback for when auto-detection doesn't catch it — the two transaction references are needed precisely because it's a duplicate-charge case, so the system needs to see both transactions to link them" [D1].

rows.question: Once NovaTel agrees to give the money back, when does it land if I paid by UPI?
rows.answer: Here is what the retrieved documents say: "The two refund destinations have different timelines because they involve different systems — refunds to source (card/UPI/net banking) depend partly on the bank's own processing time on top of NovaTel's approval, while refunds to NovaTel Wallet or account balance stay entirely within NovaTel's systems, which is why they're much faster" [D1]. "Once approved, refunds to source (card/UPI/net banking) generally reflect within 5-7 working days, subject to your bank's processing time" [D1].

rows.question: Can I get a fixed public address for my home internet so I can reach my devices remotely?
rows.answer: Here is what the retrieved documents say: "This is explicitly a paid add-on rather than a standard feature, and the answer notes the intended use case — hosting or remote access — which explains why it isn't offered as default: most home broadband use doesn't need a fixed address exposed to the internet, but specific technical use cases do" [D1]. "Static IP is available as a paid add-on on select broadband plans, primarily intended for hosting/remote-access use cases" [D1].

rows.question: Does NovaTel offer any help for customers who can't hear well?

"Account merging is supported only for connections held by the same KYC-verified individual" [D1].
